chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Isma'il, from Abi al-Subbah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a garment that one delivers to the dyer (qassār), and he ruins it. He said: 'Compensate him (charge him for the loss), for you only delivered it to him to be repaired/improved, and you did not deliver it to him to be ruined.'

key_terms.أَغْرِمْهُ: Compensate him / Charge him (for the loss)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dyer ruins a customer's garment?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on leases (*al-Ijarat*), this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *gharamah* (compensation) for damage caused by negligence or fault in a service contract. It underscores the Shia juristic view that the default intent (*asl*) of delivering an item to a craftsman is for its preservation and improvement, thereby placing the burden of proof and cost of loss on the artisan unless otherwise specified.
